q: What did King Nebuchadnezzar set up on the plain of Dura for everyone to worship?
why: Everyone was ordered to bow down to it.
quote: King Nebuchadnezzar made a golden statue

q: What would happen to anyone who did not bow to Nebuchadnezzar's golden statue?
a: Be thrown into a fiery furnace
why: The king wanted everyone to obey.
quote: will immediately be thrown into the blazing fiery furnace.

q: Which three young Jews refused to worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden statue?
why: They would worship only the true God.
quote: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego—who have ignored you, O king

q: Facing the furnace, what did Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego say their God was able to do?
why: They trusted God's power.
quote: then He is able to deliver us from the blazing fiery furnace

q: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego said that even if God did not save them, they would still never do what?
why: They would stay faithful no matter what.
quote: we will not serve your gods or worship the golden statue you have set up.

q: How much hotter did Nebuchadnezzar order the furnace for the three friends?
why: The king was filled with rage.
quote: He gave orders to heat the furnace seven times hotter than usual

q: Looking into the fiery furnace, how many men did King Nebuchadnezzar see walking in the fire?
why: Someone was with them in the fire.
quote: I see four men, unbound and unharmed, walking around in the fire

q: When the three friends came out of the fiery furnace, what was there no smell of on them?
why: Not even a hair was singed.
quote: and there was no smell of fire on them.

q: What law did King Darius's officials trick him into making to trap Daniel?
a: Pray to no one but the king
why: They knew Daniel prayed to God.
quote: that for thirty days anyone who petitions any god or man except you, O king, will be thrown into the den of lions.

q: How long was King Darius's law against praying to anyone but him supposed to last?
why: Anyone who broke it would face the lions.
quote: for thirty days

q: After the law against prayer was signed, how many times a day did Daniel keep praying?
why: He prayed just as he had done before.
quote: and three times a day he got down on his knees, prayed

q: Which way did Daniel's windows face when he prayed in Babylon?
why: Jerusalem was the city of God's temple.
quote: where the windows of his upper room opened toward Jerusalem

q: Where was Daniel thrown for praying to God?
why: King Darius could not change the law.
quote: and threw him into the den of lions.

q: When did King Darius hurry to the lions' den to check on Daniel?
a: At the first light of dawn
why: The king could not wait to know.
quote: At the first light of dawn, the king got up and hurried to the den of lions.

q: How did God protect Daniel in the lions' den?
a: His angel shut the lions' mouths
why: Daniel was innocent before God.
quote: My God sent His angel and shut the mouths of the lions.

q: Why were no wounds found on Daniel when he came out of the lions' den?
a: He had trusted in his God
why: Faith in God kept him safe.
quote: because he had trusted in his God.

q: As a young captive in Babylon, what did Daniel refuse to eat and drink?
why: He did not want to defile himself.
quote: he would not defile himself with the king’s food or wine.

q: In Babylon, what did Daniel and his friends ask to eat for ten days?
why: They asked to be tested.
quote: Let us be given only vegetables to eat and water to drink.

q: After ten days of vegetables and water, how did Daniel and his friends look?
why: God blessed their choice.
quote: they looked healthier and better nourished than all the young men

q: In Babylon, what new name was Daniel given?
why: The chief official renamed all four young men.
quote: To Daniel he gave the name Belteshazzar

q: In Babylon, what new name was Daniel's friend Hananiah given?
why: He later faced the fiery furnace.
quote: to Hananiah, Shadrach

q: Besides knowledge, what special gift did God give Daniel in Babylon?
why: This gift later helped him explain the king's dreams.
quote: And Daniel had insight into all kinds of visions and dreams.

q: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream that Daniel explained, what was the statue's head made of?
why: Each metal stood for a kingdom.
quote: The head of the statue was pure gold

q: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream that Daniel explained, what were the statue's feet made of?
why: The feet were the weak point.
quote: and its feet were part iron and part clay.

q: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream, what did the stone that struck the statue become?
why: It filled the whole earth, like God's kingdom.
quote: But the stone that had struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.

q: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream, how was the stone that crushed the statue cut out?
why: It came from God, not people.
quote: a stone was cut out, but not by human hands.

q: What signal told everyone in Babylon to bow to Nebuchadnezzar's golden statue?
why: Horns, flutes, harps, and more were played.
quote: As soon as you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipes, and all kinds of music

q: King Nebuchadnezzar said the fourth man in the fiery furnace looked like what?
why: God was with His servants in the fire.
quote: and the fourth looks like a son of the gods!

q: At King Belshazzar's feast, what appeared and wrote on the palace wall?
a: The fingers of a human hand
why: The king watched the hand writing.
quote: At that moment the fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the plaster of the wall

q: What words were written on the wall at King Belshazzar's feast?
why: Daniel explained what they meant.
quote: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, PARSIN.

q: When jealous officials looked for a charge against Daniel, what did they find?
why: Daniel was trustworthy.
quote: but they could find no charge or corruption, because he was trustworthy

q: Why did King Darius plan to set Daniel over the whole kingdom?
why: Daniel stood out among all the officials.
quote: Soon, by his extraordinary spirit, Daniel distinguished himself among the administrators and satraps.

q: As Daniel was thrown to the lions, what did King Darius say to him?
why: The king hoped Daniel's God would save him.
quote: May your God, whom you serve continually, deliver you!

q: During the reigns of which two kings did Daniel prosper?
why: God blessed Daniel's faithfulness.
quote: So Daniel prospered during the reign of Darius and the reign of Cyrus the Persian.

q: In Babylon, what new name was Daniel's friend Mishael given?
why: The chief official renamed him.
quote: to Mishael, Meshach

q: In Babylon, what new name was Daniel's friend Azariah given?
why: He was one of the three in the furnace.
quote: and to Azariah, Abednego.

q: On which plain did Nebuchadnezzar set up his golden statue?
why: It was in the province of Babylon.
quote: and he set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.

q: How high was Nebuchadnezzar's golden statue?
why: It was six cubits wide.
quote: a golden statue sixty cubits high and six cubits wide

q: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream, what were the statue's chest and arms made of?
why: The head was gold, the chest silver.
quote: its chest and arms were silver

q: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream, what were the statue's belly and thighs made of?
why: The legs were iron.
quote: its belly and thighs were bronze

q: At Belshazzar's feast, near what in the palace did the hand write on the wall?
why: The king could see it clearly.
quote: near the lampstand in the royal palace.

q: For how many days did Daniel ask to be tested on vegetables and water?
why: At the end they looked healthier than the rest.
quote: Please test your servants for ten days.
